articles.title: Arc Raiders' 2.0 Update and 'Spider-Man' Grappling Hook Drive Player Count to Reach 7-Month High
articles.summary: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.
body: Embark's once-viral extraction experience has had a rough few months. As the studio slowed down updates and vowed to rework its divisive Expedition prestige system, Arc Raiders players have largely left it behind, hoping to one day return to Speranza should more enticing updates arrive.

After reaching an all-time peak of nearly 500,000 players on Steam (via SteamDB ), it's consistently struggled to reach more than 35,000 players on PC since July. It was a fall from grace that's left fans missing the honeymoon phase, but the Frozen Trail update, which launched two days ago, October 8, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S, has almost immediately brought back some of that hype.

In September, Arc Raiders reached a player count low of just 10,000 on Steam. As of the publication of this story, 166,670 people are logged onto Arc Raiders on the PC platform alone, and it looks like it could keep climbing. It's a number Embark hasn't hit since early April, and although it's too soon to tell if these are the kind of results needed to give it a proper second wind, it does mark the first time the game has achieved a notable spike since December 2025.
points: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.

articles.title: Image Comics' Roam Reunites Paper Girls Creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang
articles.summary: In what is easily one of the most exciting comic book-related announcements to come out of NYCC 2026, IGN can exclusively reveal that Paper Girls creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang are reuniting for a new project at Image Comics.
body: “Cliff has already drawn the first several issues of ROAM, and I can’t wait for readers to see this breathtakingly original world he and our gifted collaborators Matt and Jared helped create," Vaughan tells IGN. "Thanks so much to the readers and retailers out here who are up for exploring something new with us!"

"There's no bigger thrill than breathing life into new worlds with your friends, that electric feeling of collaboration," Chiang says. "ROAM is unlike anything Brian and I have done before, but inspired by our love for comics as a medium. It's been a joy to reunite with our trusted teammates Matt Wilson and Jared Fletcher, and I'm incredibly grateful to Image Comics for continuing the creative partnership and exploration that began with Paper Girls. It's going to be a wild ride!"
Roam #1 will be released in February 2027, and it's already shaping up to be one of our most anticipated new comics of the eyar. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.
For more, check out IGN's original review of Paper Girls #1 and our review of Paper Girls Season 1.

articles.title: Forget John Wick, the Ultimate Action Thriller of the Century Is Officially Streaming on Netflix
articles.summary: Some of my favorite movies are about ordinary dudes who turn out to be a nightmare for anyone dumb enough to cross them. Pierre Morel’s Taken twisted Liam Neeson into the patron saint of revenge. Then came John Wick with an angry Keanu Reeves to perfect that very specific formula.
body: But Denzel Washington just hits different. Having starred in the 2004 masterwork of action, Man on Fire, Washington knows perfectly well how to captivate as a tired ex-soldier pushed to the brink. While it might not have the same Tony Scott flair, 2014’s The Equalizer still carries that satisfying dad-action energy — but in this film, Washington’s kills feel even more visceral at times. It may not be the pinnacle of the genre, but it’s still one of my dad’s favorites, and it just dropped on Netflix, making now the perfect time to revisit one of Washington’s best characters.

Directed by Antoine Fuqua, who previously teamed up with Washington for Training Day, The Equalizer takes inspiration from the 1980s television series of the same name. Unlike the show's private detective, who uses his particular set of skills to help people who have nowhere else to turn, Washington instead steps into the role of Robert McCall, a quiet Boston hardware store employee who spends his nights reading books at a local diner. When a teenage diner regular (Chloë Grace Moretz) runs into serious trouble with the Russian mob, McCall is forced to fold back into the person he long abandoned to protect her.

articles.title: Crystal Lake Showrunner on Retelling the Friday the 13th Story: ‘It's Always Ripe for Reinterpretation’
articles.summary: We spoke to Crystal Lake showrunner Brad Caleb Kane, star Linda Cardellini, and other cast members about retelling the Friday the 13th story.
body: Spoilers follow for the first episode of Crystal Lake, which debuts on Peacock on October 15!

The cast and creator of Crystal Lake showed up at New York Comic Con this week to prep fans for the launch of their Friday the 13th sequel series' next week. That included a panel discussion, a Camp Crystal Lake activation experience, and a screening of the first episode of the show. I also got a chance to talk to the group about the long-awaited return to the hunting grounds of Jason Voorhees… and his mom Pamela. Don’t forget about Pamela!

We’ll have a full season review of Crystal Lake in a few days, but for now I’m going to break down the biggest points from Episode 1, as well as some thoughts from showrunner Brad Caleb Kane, star Linda Cardellini, and the other cast members who were in attendance. So let’s take a swim in the lake…!

Right out of the gate, the episode gives us Linda Cardellini’s Pamela covered in blood, leaning over a bathroom sink and staring at herself in the mirror. She finds a human tooth embedded in one of her knuckles and says to herself, “What did you do…?”

articles.title: Nicolas Cage Says He'll 'Probably Not Work With' Amazon Again After Declining Spider-Noir AI Waiver
articles.summary: Nicolas Cage said he'll "probably not work with" Amazon again after declining to sign a waiver to use AI on Spider-Noir. The National Treasure actor made his position on the controversial technology clear during a New York Comic Con 2026 panel attended by IGN.
body: "Amazon is a very AI-friendly company, to the tune of $50 billion invested in OpenAI. I'm not an AI-friendly actor," Cage said. "I'm not part of their club. I didn't sign the waiver to use AI on Spider-Noir. I'll probably not work with that studio again, but that's OK."

Cage is far from a newcomer to the growing list of Hollywood talent to come out against AI in recent years. In early 2025, the actor used the Saturn Awards as an opportunity to speak against artificial intelligence, saying he's "a big believer in not letting robots dream for us."

"Robots cannot reflect the human condition for us," he continued. "That is a dead end if an actor lets one AI robot manipulate his or her performance even a little bit, an inch will eventually become a mile and all integrity, purity, and truth of art will be replaced by financial interests only. We can’t let that happen."
He also told The New Yorker that he was "terrified" of AI in 2024. Now that Cage is likely writing off working with Amazon, it sounds like he's putting his money where his mouth is.

articles.title: Naruto To Get New Manga, Crossover Anime, And More Before The End Of The Decade
articles.summary: Naruto had a big presence at New York Comic Con this year, confirming several new projects coming next year or so. These projects kick off a roadmap called Project Rasengan that runs through 2029 and includes a new crossover anime with Ninku, a new manga by series creator Masashi Kishimoto, and…
body: The panel began by unveiling the previously teased new Naruto anime, although it's not exactly what you'd expect. It's a crossover limited series anime with Ninku, aptly titled Naruto x Ninku. If you're unfamiliar with Ninku, it's the martial arts shonen manga and anime series that inspired Naruto's creator, Masashi Kishimoto.
The anime is in production. Its placement on the roadmap also suggests a 2027 release, although its teaser trailer does not confirm that outright.

Also coming in 2027 are the Naruto Card Game and a Western release of a mobile video game previously available only in China. The panel showed off art for several different cards and confirmed a simultaneous worldwide release for the base game and its first booster pack in June 2027. In-store demos for the card game will be held next February and March.

Meanwhile, Naruto Mobile is a game that has only been available in China since 2016. Bandai Namco is finally giving it a worldwide release, but it won't commit to a release window just yet, despite its proximity to 2027 on the roadmap. We'll learn more about the mobile game's worldwide release at Jump Festa 2027 this December.

articles.title: Warner Bros. 41-Year-Old Fantasy Classic Reboot is Officially Happening
articles.summary: It's been more than five years since Warner Bros. and Adam Wingard ( Godzilla vs. Kong, The Guest ) announced plans to make a live-action film adaptation of the '80s classic cartoon ThunderCats but there's been little to show for it.
body: The live-action ThunderCats movie is not dead, Wingard tells Polygon. In fact, he was working on the project in earnest earlier this year.
In an interview with Polygon, Wingard says his ThunderCats movie is still on his stack of in-development projects.

"My career's kind of bouncing around, so different things have taken precedence," Wingard says. "But [ ThunderCats is] still kicking around. I think it's just a matter of finding time to really re-concentrate and re-engage with it. We did a new draft at the beginning of this year. It wasn't too long ago, and then things got put on hold for [ Onslaught ]. So I don't really have any exciting updates.
"But it's not dead. It lives. It's just not the number one [thing] I'm working on right now."

articles.title: Strange Scaffold announces Gods With Badges, a tactics game where you decide when to switch off your bodycam
articles.summary: Strange Scaffold, the studio behind I Am Your Beast and El Paso, Elsewhere, has announced Gods With Badges, a narrative tactics game about the power police hold over life and death.
body: You play as Harrow McClellan, a disgraced police officer transferred back to her original post after the scandal that drove her out has become law enforcement legend. Every dialogue choice and turn-based encounter is a decision to play into that reputation or try to rise above it.

You'll patrol the open hubs of Scarhelm, a dystopian city of the future, seizing contraband, investigating complaints, and searching back alleys for evidence. Your dialogue choices, arrests, and uses of force shape Harrow's relationships with her fellow officers, the public, and the institutions around her.

Interestingly, when a situation escalates, the game shifts to isometric turn-based combat. Here you can take cover, rescue hostages, and decide how much force to use. You can also temporarily disable Harrow's body camera, unlocking new tactical and dialogue options but removing the public record of what happens next.

Gods With Badges began life as Hard Justice, an unrealised project from strategy studio Artificer. Strange Scaffold has built on its foundations and development materials, reinterpreting them in its own style.

articles.title: Henry Cavill's New Sci-fi Streaming Series Sets Carrie Reboot Creator to Direct
articles.summary: The grim darkness of the far future is ripe with horrors, so who is better than a legendary horror director to be attached to the upcoming Warhammer 40,000 Prime Video live-action adaptation starring Henry Cavill?
body: In Games Workshop financial report from July, Games Workshop CEO Kevin Rountree revealed that Amazon has assigned United Artists and Mike Flanagan to the Warhammer 40K adaptation: "Having completed initial outlines, Mike should soon be moving on to script," the report reads.

Flanagan is known for directing adaptations of Stephen King works such as Gerald's Game and Doctor Sleep, as well as Netflix horror series The Haunting of Hill House, The Haunting of Bly Manor, Midnight Mass, and The Fall of the House of Usher. His next projects include another King adaptation, Prime Video's Carrie, and DC Studios' Clayface.

There are no details about the timeline for the project, and Games Workshop's report states that "these adaptations will take years to bring successfully to market." At least, the mention of adaptations, plural, hints that the partnership with Amazon will produce more than one movie or series.

articles.title: Squadron 42 has a Steam page
articles.summary: In August, game director Chris Roberts said that Star Citizen's singleplayer component, Squadron 42, was being delayed out of 2026 to avoid clashing with Grand Theft Auto 6.
body: There's also a new trailer, which leans heavily on the oorah stuff that's always a bit of a turn-off in military science-fiction. Privateer was my favorite Wing Commander game because it left out all the Top Gun nonsense, but of course it's front-and-center in Squadron 42.

So too are the celebrity actors, with appearances by Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Rhona Mitra, that guy who played the Onion Knight in Game of Thrones, and other people who probably filmed most of their scenes a solid decade ago now. We also get to see a fair bit of the male version of the player-character, who will doubtless BroShep his way into most of the promos even though I'll be picking the one voiced by Alix Wilton Regan instead.

The Steam page lists Squadron 42's release date as Q2 2027, and I'd love to see it actually release on that date and be the solid combo of Wing Commander and Half-Life 2 that happens to have Gillian Anderson and Henry Cavill in the cutscenes that's being promised here. It could happen.

articles.title: GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is now reportedly threatening to release a full, playable build of the game
articles.summary: A GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to put out a complete, playable build of the game, start to finish.
body: The threat was posted on CyberLeek's website after the leaker shared 25 minutes of footage from the game earlier this week.

Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company, has been hunting for the person behind the leaks, and has tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

After going quiet for a bit, CyberLeek came back with a bang this week, posting new footage from Rockstar's upcoming game that even features nude scenes, including a fully naked Jason, and a topless Lucia. Eurogamer has seen the video, and it appears to be legitimate - and, as is now traditional, has CyberLeek's emblem overlaid on top of the footage.
CyberLeek now reportedly says the build will go out if their cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million, and claims it can be played through to the end credits.

articles.title: Deadlock surpasses Team Fortress 2's all-time concurrent player count peak as it adds a chess wizard
articles.summary: Valve's latest MOBA might still technically be conducting an invite-only test, but it's nevertheless one of the most popular games of its ilk. Yesterday, right as the game added the latest in its current batch of six new democratically released heroes, its concurrent player-count hit a new…
body: While that's pretty impressive on its face, it'll be especially noteworthy to long-time fans of Valve's games that this surge of activity brought Deadlock past Team Fortress 2's all-time concurrent player count peak of 253,997.

Though this doesn't include the player numbers TF2 saw on the Xbox 360 and PS3 as part of The Orange Box, which I'm sure were positively through the roof, it's still conceivably its genuine peak given that it was just three years ago. As for how TF2's history of botting issues and idle servers might have affected that number, I can't say.

It's not a one-to-one—PC gaming was a smaller phenomenon overall when TF2 was at the height of its popularity, and its Quake-descended slapstick arguably appeals to a smaller crowd than a hero shooter-MOBA hybrid does today—but it's an impressive showing for Deadlock given that the MOBA space is notoriously hard to break into.

I guess that's the power of having a digital storefront so massive that you can afford to perform mad science experiments on a game for multiple years without making a single cent off of it directly. Not that things always go this way for Valve; remember Artifact?

articles.title: The studio behind Star Wars Zero Company is bringing back some of its furloughed staff
articles.summary: Just as Star Wars Zero Company was set to launch earlier this year, developer Bit Reactor furloughed over 80% of its staff over sales uncertainty. In other words, much of its staff were receiving no pay, despite technically being employees, right when players were getting their hands on the game.
body: Bit Reactor CEO Greg Foertsch said in the statement that the decision was made in response to "unexpected business developments outside of our control," but that it was "necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible."

According to Game File, an unnamed source "familiar with the situation" has said that the developer's payroll is back up to more than half what it was before the furloughs. When this first happened, Game File reported that 80 percent of Bit Reactor employees were affected, hamstringing any sort of support following the game's release, and that the decision fell with Bit Reactor, not publisher EA.

While the launch had some issues, some of the most prominent of which were addressed in a patch shortly after release, the game shot up the Steam best seller's list and got a glowing review from PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield, who called it "a new all-timer Star Wars game and a stunning debut for Bit Reactor."

articles.title: Silent Hill, Gravity Rush director's Bokeh Game Studio is reportedly casting for a new horror game
articles.summary: It looks like Bokeh Game Studio, founded by Keiichiro Toyama, who directed the original Silent Hill and created Siren and Gravity Rush, is working on another horror game.
body: According to MP1st, Bokeh is hiring motion capture performers for its next project, which is seemingly still untitled.
The casting sheet lists characters including River, Dean, Lyra, Hazel, Becca, Dena, and Emma, plus an eight-year-old girl.

Descriptions cover mature themes including drug use and trafficking, violence, abuse, grief, and sex work, with several characters tied to creature transformation - all of which sounds surprisingly close to Toyama's prior game, Slitterhead… which is interesting, given Slitterhead didn't exactly set the world alight.
River's entry cites River Phoenix and Kurt Cobain as visual references, while Lyra's points to Mia Goth as a tonal reference.

articles.title: Gargantuan cop immersive sim Militsioner now has an acrophobia-inducing demo, and yes, I did somehow manage to fail the tutorial
articles.summary: Excitedly, I boot up the new demo for Militsioner, a game I've had a watchful eye on since its announcement. A phone rings, it's my lawyer. I don't know why I've been arrested, but with the shattering of my balcony window I quickly know one thing: there's a giant motherf**king cop that won't let me…
body: Militsioner, for the uninitiated, is an immersive sim of massive proportions. For some reason, you've been stuck in some town alongside a handful of other folks, an open air prison essentially. Your crime? Well, you're not sure really, but the giant cop constantly looming over you certainly seems to think you should know. Of course, you immediately begin to plot your escape, potentially via a train car that leads you out of town, but it's not that easy. First you have to get a job, and to get that job you need to find some desert, except, oh, what's this? A creepy character only referred to as Friend invites you into the sewer, away from the gaze of the panopticop? Fine, I'll take a look.

videos.summary: The Nintendo Switch Sports Resort game launches October 22, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2 system. Pre-orders are available now:
body: The latest game in the intuitive sports series is coming to Nintendo Switch 2!
Get moving solo or with family and friends across 12 immersive sports. Aim for the target’s center in Archery, knock down pins in Bowling, duke it out in Boxing, and more!
You can also explore the island! Use Joy-Con 2 mouse controls in Skateboarding, steer across the waves in Power Cruising, and tilt the controller to fly around freely in Prop Plane.

videos.summary: Valor Mortis releases on October 13th. Valor Mortis is a first-person action soulslike from the creators of Ghostrunner. Rise from death as a former soldier of Napoleon’s army. Wield supernatural powers, battle horrifying monsters, and unravel a conspiracy that threatens all of humanity.
